# Results — Study 692 (Breakaway Candles)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
five-candle **breakaway**: a long trend candle, a clean gap, a two-candle "run" further in
that direction, then a long reversal candle that closes back **through the gap** —
supposedly marks the end of the trend it interrupted, in *either* direction. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Panel fingerprint
`9693c3ea7807`; sample data stamp `[data] SPY OHLCV (sample): 6,280 rows 2001-07-10 ->
2026-06-30 as-of 2026-06-30 fingerprint=85f86a841de4`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLCV, SPY + 60 long-listed US large-caps (the same fixed basket as sibling studies 685/687), ~25.0 years/name, 383,080 total bars, as-of 2026-06-30 |
| Detector | **loose cut**: downtrend/uptrend context + long candle 1 + a clean gap (>= 0.5%) + a strictly monotone 2-day run + a long reversal candle closing back through the gap-day's own high/low. **Strict cut**: bigger gap (>= 1.2%), genuinely long bodies (>= 55% of range) on candles 1 & 5, and a *full* gap fill (closes back past candle 1's own extreme) |
| Base rate | the same directional bet (long after a downtrend / short after an uptrend) on every bar sharing the trend context, whether or not the five-candle shape fired |
| Statistics | Welch *t* of the reversal mean vs the base-rate mean (decisive), one-sample Newey-West HAC *t* where n permits, a 2,000-draw label-shuffle placebo, a Bonferroni-corrected critical \|*t*\| for 4 simultaneous horizons; below **n = 8** pooled events a *t*-stat is not computed at all |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: the breakaway confirms at candle 5's close; the trade enters the **next session's open**; one-way cost 5 bps/leg, one round trip = 10 bps; shorts are already sign-flipped into "trade P&L", no separate borrow line |
| Data quirks (named) | 27 bullish + 17 bearish loose events over 61 names / 25 years — a genuinely rare shape (six independent conditions must line up); the strict cut fires only **5** times basket-wide (below the n=8 test floor at every horizon) |

**Survivorship, named on the Signal axis:** the basket is all *still-trading* large-caps
(all still listed today) — for a single-pattern event study this affects which *names*
contribute events, not the direction of the loose-vs-base-rate comparison, but it is
worth naming plainly.

## The headline — combined (bullish + bearish) loose cut vs the trend-matched base rate

Both directions are pooled into one test (returns already sign-adjusted to "trade
P&L") — this is the pre-registered primary test, because the claim is bidirectional.

| H (days) | n | reversal (bps) | win % | base rate (bps) | delta (bps) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps, bps) |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 44 | **−57.1** | 43.2 | −0.2 | −56.8 | **−2.16** | 0.993 | −67.1 |
| 5 | 44 | +13.6 | 43.2 | +1.1 | +12.5 | +0.24 | 0.409 | +3.6 |
| 10 | 44 | +113.6 | 63.6 | +0.4 | +113.2 | +1.44 | 0.070 | +103.6 |
| 20 | 44 | +325.8 | 56.8 | +6.7 | +319.1 | **+2.39** | 0.002 | +315.8 |

**Bonferroni-corrected critical \|*t*\| for 4 horizons: 2.50.** No horizon clears it —
the closest is day 20 at *t* = 2.39, and the nearest naive-significant cell (day 1) is
**negative**: the breakaway's own first session gives back 57 bps against a flat base
rate before "working" at all. Under the pre-registered, bidirectional headline test, the
figure is **not statistically distinguishable from the trend-matched base rate at any
horizon**.

## Strict cut — the literature-closer breakaway

| H (days) | n | reversal (bps) | delta (bps) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 5 | −168.2 | −168.0 | n/a (n<8) | 0.993 |
| 5 | 5 | −318.6 | −319.5 | n/a (n<8) | 0.979 |
| 10 | 5 | −82.2 | −82.5 | n/a (n<8) | 0.640 |
| 20 | 5 | +587.7 | +581.1 | n/a (n<8) | 0.041 |

Five events basket-wide in 25 years — below the desk's own **n = 8** floor for computing
a *t*-stat at all. A large point estimate on five events is exactly the kind of number
the desk refuses to certify: interesting to look at, impossible to trust.

## Per-side breakdown — the desk's own symmetry myth-check

A real bidirectional reversal figure should work on *both* sides on its own merits.
It doesn't:

**Bullish breakaway** (downtrend → long), n = 27

| H | n | reversal (bps) | base (bps) | delta (bps) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 27 | −116.2 | +2.8 | −119.0 | **−3.43** | 1.000 |
| 5 | 27 | +42.2 | +27.7 | +14.5 | +0.19 | 0.414 |
| 10 | 27 | +256.4 | +55.5 | +200.9 | **+2.15** | 0.026 |
| 20 | 27 | +670.8 | +120.0 | +550.8 | **+3.33** | 0.001 |

**Bearish breakaway** (uptrend → short), n = 17

| H | n | reversal (bps) | base (bps) | delta (bps) | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 17 | +36.8 | −2.6 | +39.4 | +1.39 | 0.096 |
| 5 | 17 | −31.9 | −19.6 | −12.3 | −0.18 | 0.567 |
| 10 | 17 | −113.2 | −42.5 | −70.6 | −0.57 | 0.743 |
| 20 | 17 | −222.1 | −81.5 | −140.6 | −0.93 | 0.814 |

Split by side, **bullish 20d** nominally clears both the naive (2.0) and this
split's own Bonferroni bar (2.50) at *t* = **+3.33** — but this is an *un-pre-registered*
extra look (the headline test was the pooled, bidirectional one), it is directly
contradicted by its own **day-1 reaction** (*t* = −3.43, sharply negative — the position
first goes *against* the trade for a full session), and the **bearish** mirror shows
**nothing at any horizon** (all \|*t*\| < 1.4, and *negative* point estimates at 3 of 4
horizons) — a genuine reversal figure would not be one-sided like this.

## Is it the candle, or the calendar? — best/worst confirmed bullish breakaways (20d)

| ticker | block (candle 1 → candle 5) | 20-day forward |
|---|---|--:|
| BDX | 2002-06-11 → 2002-06-17 | **−1,792.7 bps** |
| BDX | 2011-08-17 → 2011-08-23 | −598.1 bps |
| LOW | 2002-07-18 → 2002-07-24 | +1,584.6 bps |
| DIS | 2025-04-03 → 2025-04-09 | +1,821.9 bps |
| CAT | 2010-08-23 → 2010-08-27 | **+2,026.0 bps** |

Three of the five best/worst events (LOW 2002-07, DIS 2025-04, and CAT sits weeks after
the 2010-08 correction low) land within days of famous **market-wide** lows — the
2002 post-dot-com bottom, the April-2025 tariff-selloff bottom, the 2010 "flash-crash"
correction — not obviously the candle shape itself. The same confound sibling study
687-ladder-bottom found on its own strict cut.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is (mostly) unbiased

Deterministic bar-by-bar generator with forced 5-bar breakaway blocks (alternating
bullish/bearish) and a TUNABLE planted post-reversal drift; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.58** (sd 0.90), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = 0.02 (n=99) | **+4.43** |
| planted edge = 0.04 (n=100) | **+7.96** |

The detector clearly recovers a planted reversal drift. The null is not perfectly
clean — a mild positive mean and 2 of 20 seeds crossing \|*t*\| ≥ 2, a modestly elevated
false-positive rate we attribute to the small, deliberately rare event counts the
detector produces even in a 40-name/3,500-day synthetic panel. **This is a
faithful-engine / power check only, never cited in support of the real-tape stamp** —
and it is disclosed here rather than swept under the rug, in the same spirit as every
other honesty rail on this desk.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The pre-registered, bidirectional headline test does not clear the
  Bonferroni-corrected bar (\|*t*\| ≥ 2.50) at **any** of the 4 horizons — closest is
  day 20 (*t* = 2.39), and day 1 is a **negative**, uncorrected-significant reaction
  (*t* = −2.16). The strict, literature-closer cut fires only **5** times basket-wide —
  too few to test at all. A secondary, non-pre-registered split (bullish side alone,
  20 days, *t* = +3.33) *does* clear the bar, but fails three honesty checks at once:
  it wasn't the planned primary test, its own day-1 reaction is sharply negative
  (*t* = −3.43), and its best events cluster on famous market-wide bottoms rather than a
  name-specific candle signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** 44 loose events over 61 names and 25 years — about once per
  35 ticker-years — is a curiosity, not a strategy; the strict cut is rarer still. Where
  the point estimate is positive (10d, 20d) it nominally survives a 10 bps round trip,
  so costs aren't the binding constraint — the near-absent event frequency, the missing
  certification and the day-1 whipsaw are.
- **Works both directions equally? — BUSTED.** The bullish side rides a suggestive,
  uncertified bounce concentrated in a handful of market-wide crash-bottom dates; the
  bearish mirror shows nothing at any horizon (three of four point estimates are
  negative). A real reversal figure should not need the market to be crashing in its
  favor to "work" on only one side.
